26	
27	| # | Risque | Gravité | Ce qui le traite |
28	|---|---|---|---|
29	| R1 | **Faux « no result » sur Nexus.** `_catalog` est appelé à la racine de l'hôte. Si Nexus n'y renvoie pas les noms préfixés par le dépôt membre (`docker-hosted/api`), le filtre par `repo_prefix` ne garde rien, et le registre affiche « no result » au lieu de « unsupported ». Un faux négatif trompe plus qu'un refus. Non vérifiable sans Nexus (IS-16). | Haute | Si le catalogue répond mais qu'**aucun** nom ne porte le préfixe de l'entrée (avant le filtre sur la saisie), le verdict est « unsupported or refused », avec une ligne de journal. À ajouter à IS-03. |
30	| R2 | **Réponses tardives.** `AddRegistryTags` n'a aucun identifiant de recherche. Une réponse de la recherche N-1 s'ajoute donc à la recherche N et décrémente son `pendingSearches`. Le défaut existe déjà pour les tags et toucherait les deux niveaux. | Haute | Génération (`gen int`) sur chaque message de recherche et de tags, ignorée si périmée (IS-04 c.4, IS-09 c.2). |
31	| R3 | **Délai non borné.** `ociHTTPClient` et `registryHTTPClient` ont `Timeout: 15s` par requête. Un parcours de 100 pages (`maxTagPages`) peut donc durer 25 min. Aucun `context` dans `internal/oci`. | Haute | Variantes avec `ctx` (`http.NewRequestWithContext`), une échéance par registre, et l'annulation à la nouvelle recherche ou à la fermeture du browser (`CancelFunc` détenue dans `Update`, sur le modèle de `pullOneImageCmd`). |
32	| R4 | **Erreurs non typées.** `registryGET` rend `"registry returned %d"` et `exchangeBearerToken` rend `"token endpoint returned %d"`. IS-12 exige 401/403/404/405 → refused, et 429/5xx/délai/corps illisible → failed. | Moyenne | `oci.StatusError{Code}` et classification par `errors.As`, plus `net.Error.Timeout()` ou `context.DeadlineExceeded`. Rétrocompatible pour `ListRegistryTags`. |
33	| R5 | **En-tête trop étroit pour IS-13.** La colonne d'infos fait `(largeur-2)/4` cellules : 19 à 80 colonnes, 29 à 120. Elle tient 7 lignes, et une valeur trop longue y est **coupée en silence** (`MaxWidth`, `app_header.go`), sans `+N`. La vue ne connaît pas cette largeur : `GetHeaderInfo(context)` ne la reçoit pas. | Moyenne | Exporter la formule (ex. `shortcut.InfoColumnWidth(w)`) au lieu de la recopier, prévoir une ligne par classe de verdict, et abréger dans la vue. |
34	| R6 | **Colonnes figées au premier registre.** `datatable` ne se mesure seul qu'au premier remplissage non vide (`measuredOnce`). Les lignes Nexus arrivées après Hub sont tronquées aux largeurs de Hub. | Moyenne | `Remeasure()` à chaque arrivée d'un registre tant que la recherche tourne, plus rien ensuite. Le compromis (colonnes qui bougent pendant le chargement) est assumé. |
35	| R7 | **Curseur indexé.** Le curseur de `datatable` est un index (`rebuild`). Des lignes insérées au-dessus, par tri ou par arrivée, changent la ligne sélectionnée. | Moyenne | Côté vue : retenir la clé (`EntryKey`+`Repo`), puis `SetCursor` après `SetItems`. Ne pas toucher `datatable`. |
36	| R8 | **« Sans étoiles en dernier dans les deux sens » (IS-05 c.3)** est impossible avec `Less` seul : `sorted()` inverse le comparateur en descendant. | Basse | Petite extension transverse de `datatable` (ex. `Column.Missing func(T) bool`), ou critère abandonné. |
37	| R9 | **Deux barres de filtre.** Le niveau 2 garde sa barre maison (`filterInput` + `FilterBarView`, déjà en écart avec Rule 136). Le niveau 1 doit prendre celle de `datatable`. Le pied OCI (`view.go` l.56, l.82) et `InEditMode` doivent suivre le niveau actif. | Basse | Aiguillage par état dans `FilterIsVisible`/`FilterBarView`/`InEditMode`. Le niveau 2 n'est pas corrigé (non-objectif). |
38	| R10 | **Hub + `repo_prefix` est déjà incohérent** : `joinRepoPrefix("bitnami", "library/nginx")`. | Basse | Hypothèse : l'adaptateur Hub ignore le préfixe, ou ne garde que les noms `prefix/…`. À noter, pas à corriger ici. |
39	| R11 | **Contrat Hub v1 non garanti** : endpoint non documenté côté Hub, limite de débit anonyme inconnue. | Basse (vérifié aujourd'hui) | URL dans une variable de paquet (faux Hub en test), 429 → failed, une seule page. |
40	
41	Points irréversibles : aucun (pas de format persistant nouveau, pas de migration de config).
42	La seule écriture persistante reste `browser_selection.go`, inchangée.
43	
44	## 2. Effort par story
45	
46	| Story | Effort | Justification (une ligne) |
47	|---|---|---|
48	| IS-01 | **M** (était S) | Embarque le squelette du niveau 1 : état `browserStateImages`, table, `ActivityTables`, aide, compteur d'en-tête, aiguillage `/`, avertissement « No registry selected ». L'avertissement est aujourd'hui un `return b, nil` silencieux quand aucune commande n'est lancée. |
49	| IS-02 | **S** (était M) | Une fois le squelette dans IS-01, l'adaptateur Hub est un GET et un décodage JSON vérifié, avec `library/` via `normalizeRepoForRegistry` et une URL remplaçable en test. |
50	| IS-03 | **M** | `oci.ListCatalog` (pagination `Link` déjà sue par `resolveNext`, plafond, `ctx`), filtre préfixe puis sous-chaîne, et garde R1. Testable entièrement en `httptest`. |
51	| IS-04 | **S** | Génération (R2), `LoadingLabel` étendu au niveau 1, `Remeasure` par arrivée (R6), statut de pied pour la ligne sélectionnée. |
52	| IS-05 | **S + S** | Le tri `.` est gratuit (`CycleSort`, et « no sort » est un arrêt du cycle quand `SortColumn` vaut -1). Le c.3 demande l'extension R8 ; le c.5 relève de R7. |
53	| IS-06 | **M** (était S) | La recherche `/` est gratuite (`Search` sur Name et Description). En revanche `filterStops` est câblé sur `b.tags`, donc à généraliser, et le jeton de registre doit vivre dans la barre de `datatable`, dont les jetons sont fixés à `New`. |
54	| IS-07 | **S** | Regrouper les cibles par (URL d'API, identifiants), un parcours, puis répartir par préfixe. Repose sur une hypothèse Nexus non vérifiée. |
55	| IS-08 | **M** | Un seul `searchRegistryTagsCmd` avec le `Repo` final de la ligne, **sans** renormaliser (préfixe et `library/` déjà appliqués). La matrice de références docker/podman/préfixe est à tester. |
56	| IS-09 | **S** | La table du niveau 1 reste en mémoire pendant le niveau 2 : curseur, tri et filtre sont conservés sans pile. Plus un drapeau d'origine (`tagsFromSearch`) pour `esc`. |
57	| IS-10 | **S** (XS) | Une fois Q2 tranchée, quelle que soit l'interprétation : soit `enter` = `→`, soit l'agrégation de scan (§7). |
58	| IS-11 | **S** | Un second bouton dans le formulaire : les indices `brFieldSubmit` se décalent et l'en-tête grise selon le focus. |
59	| IS-12 | **M** | R4 (erreurs typées dans `internal/oci`), une fonction pure `Classify`, neuf cas `httptest`, aucun `err.Error()` à l'écran. |
60	| IS-13 | **M** (était S) | R5 : budget de l'en-tête inconnu de la vue, abréviation `+N`, compte des registres en attente. |
61	| IS-14 | **S** | Libellé dérivé de `provider`/`kind`/`ParentSlug`. Aucun appel réseau. |
62	| IS-15 | **S** (XS) | `commands.go:436` compare l'URL brute ; il suffit de la remplacer par `isDockerHub`. C'est la seule comparaison brute du paquet (l'autre occurrence est `isDockerHub` lui-même). |
63	| IS-16 | **S** à valider, **non borné** à corriger | Si Nexus contredit l'hypothèse « préfixe dans `_catalog` », IS-03 et IS-07 sont à reprendre. |
64	| IS-17 | non estimé | Aucune API connue (inchangé). |
65	
66	## 3. Redécoupage et ordre
67	
68	- **Redistribuer IS-01 et IS-02.** IS-01 ne se démontre pas sans niveau 1 (c.1). IS-01 porte donc
69	  le squelette, avec une recherche injectable (faux `Searcher`). IS-02 ne porte plus que
70	  l'adaptateur Hub et ses colonnes de métadonnées.
71	- **Le c.1 d'IS-05 (ordre par défaut déterministe) passe dans le MVP**, avec IS-04. Sans lui,
72	  l'ordre des lignes dépend de l'ordre d'arrivée des registres, donc varie d'une recherche à
73	  l'autre. IS-05 garde le tri `.` et le c.3 (R8).
74	- **Ajouter à IS-03** la garde R1 et l'échéance par registre (R3). **Ajouter à IS-04** la
75	  génération (R2).
76	- **Corriger IS-02 c.5** : à 60 colonnes il reste la colonne d'activité, Name et Registry
77	  (voir §5). Ordre des colonnes : Name, Registry, Stars, Official, Description. Placée à droite,
78	  Description cède la première (sinon, `DropFirst`).
79	- **Signaler à IS-08 c.7** que « comme aujourd'hui » veut dire *silencieux à l'écran* :
80	  `handleMultiRegistryTagsLoaded` ne fait que journaliser l'échec. Il faut décider si le niveau 2
81	  ouvert depuis le niveau 1 dit au moins quelque chose dans le pied de page (`Error`).
82	
83	Ordre recommandé (→ = dépend de) :
84	
85	1. **IS-15** : indépendante, à tout moment. À faire tôt, parce qu'IS-02 s'appuie sur `isDockerHub`.
86	2. **IS-12a, socle** (`oci.StatusError`, `Classify`, génération, `ctx`). Peut se fusionner dans IS-01.
87	3. **IS-01** (squelette) → 2.
88	4. **IS-02** (Hub) → 3. **IS-04** + ordre par défaut → 3. *Parallélisables.*
89	5. **IS-08** → 4, puis **IS-09** → 5. On a alors une tranche Hub de bout en bout.
90	6. **IS-12** (états à l'écran) → 2, 3. **IS-13** → 6.
91	7. **IS-03** → 6 (les verdicts existent). **IS-14** → 7.
92	8. Should : **IS-11** (dépend seulement du formulaire, parallélisable dès 3), **IS-05** → 4,
93	   **IS-06** → 4, **IS-07** → 7, **IS-10** → Q2.
94	
95	## 4. Composants et interfaces probables
96	
97	**Nouveau paquet `internal/imagesearch`** (Go pur, sans UI, testable seul) :
98	
99	- `Target{EntryKey, RegistryURL, APIURL, RepoPrefix, Provider, Kind, Username, Password}` et
100	  `Query{Text string; Limit int}`.
101	- `Image{EntryKey, Name, Repo, Description string; Stars int; HasStars, Official bool}`.
102	  `Name` est ce que la table affiche ; `Repo` est le chemin final (préfixe et `library/` appliqués
103	  une fois, D39), celui qu'IS-08 passe tel quel au lister de tags.
104	- `Searcher` : `Search(ctx, Target, Query) (images []Image, partial bool, err error)`.
105	  - `hubSearcher` : `index.docker.io/v1/search`, toujours anonyme.
106	  - `catalogSearcher` : `oci.ListCatalog`, filtre préfixe puis sous-chaîne insensible à la casse
107	    sur la partie après le préfixe (Hypothèse : sinon `host` trouverait tout `docker-hosted/…`),
108	    garde R1.
109	  - Plus tard, un adaptateur par `provider` (harbor, nexus, …) derrière la même interface.
110	- `For(Target) Searcher` : Hub est reconnu par `isDockerHub(url)`, comme partout dans le code
111	  existant ; tout le reste prend le catalogue. Le `provider` n'est lu qu'au-delà du MVP.
112	  `isDockerHub` est à déplacer ou exposer hors de `oci_resources`, sinon la logique est dupliquée.
113	- `Verdict` (OK, NoResult, Refused, Failed), `Outcome{Verdict; Partial bool; Count int}` et
114	  `Classify(err, n, partial) Outcome`, une fonction pure.
115	- `Rank(query, []Image) []Image` : l'ordre par défaut (Q3).
116	
117	**`internal/oci`** : `ListCatalog(ctx, apiURL, user, pass string, maxPages, pageSize int) (repos []string, truncated bool, err error)`,
118	`StatusError{Code int}`, et des variantes `ctx` de `registryGET`/`registryDo`. Le défi Bearer
119	reste celui d'aujourd'hui : le `scope` vient du défi, donc `registry:catalog:*`.
120	
121	**UI (`internal/ui/oci_resources`)**. Fichiers **nommés `browser_*.go`** : la surface clavier
122	`oci/browser` (`keymap.go` l.219) n'autorise `r` que sous ce préfixe.
123	
124	- Un sous-état `imageSearch` porté par `RegistryBrowser` : génération, `pending`, la table du
125	  niveau 1 et `outcomes map[entryKey]Outcome`, plus `cancel` pour l'annulation.
126	- `ImageSearchResultMsg{Gen, EntryKey, Images, Outcome}`, routé par `Model.Update` vers un
127	  `handle…` de `browser_bridge.go`, comme `MultiRegistryTagsLoadedMsg`.
128	
129	**Modèle à deux niveaux, comparé à l'explorer** :
130	
131	- L'explorer n'a **qu'une** table de `TreeNode`. Il remplace ses lignes à chaque niveau et
132	  garde `navigationStack` et `cursorStack`. `←` et `esc` appellent tous deux `handleDrillUp`
133	  (`update.go` l.190-195).
134	- Le browser a deux niveaux de **types différents** (`imageRow`, `tagRow`). Il garde donc
135	  **deux tables**, et l'état devient Input → Images → Tags. La table du niveau 1 n'est jamais
136	  vidée pendant le niveau 2 : pas de pile, et IS-09 c.1 est satisfait par construction.
137	
138	**État par registre dans l'en-tête** : il est porté par `imageSearch.outcomes`, dans le browser.
139	`Model.GetHeaderInfo` (`view.go` l.243) le lit pour l'état Images seulement ; l'état Tags garde
140	`Tags: N` (IS-13 c.6). Lignes proposées, sur 7 au plus :
141	
142	- `Images: N` ;
143	- `Pending: 2` ;
144	- une ligne par verdict non nul : `Failed: dhi.io +1`, `Refused: nexus-prod`, `Partial: hub`.
145	
146	L'abréviation `+N` se calcule avec la largeur exportée (R5).
147	
148	## 5. Ce qu'exigent le garde d'activité et les règles 116, 128, 136, 139
149	
150	- **`activity_guard_test.go`.** La vue OCI est « migrée », donc elle ne peut pas être exemptée,
151	  et le garde n'a pas d'exemption par table. Ce qu'il vérifie, et seulement si la table est
152	  déclarée :
153	  - la table est listée dans `migratedTables` (ex. `"oci/registry-search"`) **et** rapportée par
154	    `ActivityTables()`, le browser ouvert ou non. Le modèle est `newTagTable()` redimensionné
155	    dans `activity.go` ;
156	  - colonne 0 = `datatable.IndicatorColumn` : sans titre, `SizingFixed`, `IconColumnWidth`,
157	    sans `Less` ni `Search` ;
158	  - `RenderedWidth() == 58` à 60 colonnes ;
159	  - la section `indicator.Legend` dans l'aide, déjà présente.
160	
161	  Une table omise ne fait **pas** échouer le garde. Ce serait pourtant un trou que la revue
162	  relèverait (Rule 125). Recommandation : déclarer la table, avec une colonne d'activité
163	  toujours `Idle` qui affiche au repos `IconDocker`, rôle `IconRoleImage`, comme l'onglet
164	  Images. Elle coûte 4 cellules. Ajouter aussi les nouveaux fichiers à `migratedSources` : sinon
165	  ils échappent à l'analyse des mécanismes retirés, sans que rien n'échoue. Pas de `tea.Tick`
166	  dans ces fichiers ; `spinner.Tick` est permis. Pas de nouveau « footer seed » requis.
167	- **Rule 116.** Chaque colonne déclare son `Sizing`. Description et Stars sont
168	  `Optional`+`YieldsToContent`, Official aussi. On teste `RenderedWidth() == largeur-2` à
169	  plusieurs largeurs. À 60 colonnes restent ●, Name et Registry.
170	- **Rule 128.**
171	  - « Searching registries... » avec le spinner dans le pied (le `LoadingLabel` existant, étendu
172	    à l'état Images).
173	  - Après la recherche, le pied décrit la ligne sélectionnée (référence complète et registre).
174	  - Un échec : journal `ERROR [oci_resources]` sans identifiant (voir `jobs.SafeCause`), un
175	    éventuel `Error` de 3 s, et le verdict **persistant dans l'en-tête**. Jamais de
176	    `err.Error()` à l'écran.
177	  - « No registry selected » est un `Warn`.
178	- **Rule 136.** Le niveau 1 utilise la `FilterBar` de `datatable`, et non une copie de la barre
179	  maison du niveau 2. `GetFooterHeight` ajoute `ExtraHeight()` de la barre du niveau actif ;
180	  `InEditMode` propage `table.InEditMode()` (sinon `:` ouvre la palette pendant la saisie) ; `esc`
181	  ferme d'abord la barre (IS-09 c.5).
182	- **Rule 139.** Le corps reste toujours `table.View()` : en cours, vide, ou filtré à zéro. Aucune
183	  ligne factice pour un verdict (cohérent avec Q6). Le compte va dans `GetHeaderInfo`.
184	- Aussi : Rule 130 (le raccourci `→` est grisé sans ligne sous le curseur, et `enter` est grisé
185	  tant que Q2 n'est pas tranchée), Rule 114 (aide mise à jour dans le même commit), Rule 122
186	  (cellules en texte brut, `Official` en mot).
187	
188	## 6. Points de la recherche encore non vérifiés qui menacent le MVP
189	
190	1. **Noms renvoyés par `_catalog` sur Nexus** : préfixés par le dépôt membre ou non, selon
191	   l'URL appelée (hôte, connecteur, chemin `repository/<groupe>`). C'est R1. Cela conditionne
192	   IS-03 c.2, IS-07 et la confiance dans « no result ».
193	2. **Droits de `_catalog` pour un compte de pull Nexus** : refus (→ « refused », acceptable) ou
194	   liste partielle silencieuse (→ faux négatif).
195	3. **Comportement de `dhi.io` sur `_catalog`.** Un 200 avec une liste vide ou partielle
196	   s'afficherait « no result ». Recommandation : tant qu'IS-17 n'est pas faite, ne pas traiter
197	   `dhi.io` comme les autres (« unsupported » d'office). Sinon, accepter le risque.
198	4. **Pagination réelle du catalogue** (`n` respecté, plafonné ou ignoré). Le corps reste borné
199	   par `maxTagResponse` (32 MiB).
200	5. **Hub v1** : limite de débit anonyme inconnue. Les champs et le plafond de 100 sont, eux,
201	   vérifiés le 2026-11-10.
202	6. **Mention « cached content only » de Nexus proxy** (IS-14) : source secondaire seulement.
203	
204	## 7. Questions ouvertes Q3 à Q10, et l'ambiguïté Q2
205	
206	**Q2, ambiguïté à faire trancher par l'utilisateur.** Le code établit ceci :
207	
208	- au **niveau 2**, `enter` appelle `openTagScanDetails` (`browser_tags.go` l.144) et ouvre
209	  `ScanDetailsRequestMsg` seulement si `scanCache[multiImageName(url, repo, tag)]` existe ;
210	  sinon `return b, nil` en silence, la touche étant grisée (`view.go` l.307) ;
211	- le cache de scan est indexé par **référence complète avec tag**.
212	
213	Une ligne du niveau 1 n'a pas de tag, donc pas de clé de scan. La phrase de l'utilisateur colle
214	mot pour mot au comportement **actuel du niveau 2**, à conserver tel quel (IS-08 c.2). Deux
215	lectures restent possibles :
216	
217	- **(A)** elle décrit le niveau 2. IS-10 reste ouverte pour le niveau 1 (`enter` = `→`, ou rien).
218	- **(B)** elle vise le niveau 1. Il faut alors un **scan agrégé par image** : chercher dans le
219	  cache les clés `<ref sans tag>:*` en tenant compte de `library/` et de `docker.io/` sous
220	  podman, et choisir lequel ouvrir (le plus récent par `ScannedAt`, qui existe). Cela grise
221	  `enter` sans scan, et rouvre de fait Q8, que les stories excluent.
222	
223	Effort : S pour (A), S à M pour (B). Non tranché ici.
224	
225	**Q3, ordre par défaut.** *Factuel :*
226	
227	- `datatable` accepte « aucun tri » (`SortColumn: -1`) avec l'ordre fourni par la vue, et
228	  `CycleSort` y revient. L'ordre par défaut est donc une fonction pure côté vue (`Rank`), sans
229	  toucher `datatable`.
230	- Hub renvoie son propre ordre de pertinence (officielle en tête pour `nginx`) ; il est perdu au
231	  mélange.
232	
233	*Avis :* nom égal à la saisie, puis commençant par, puis contenant ; à égalité, alphabétique,
234	puis par alias de registre. Stars seulement via `.`.
235	
236	**Q4, Hub anonyme ou authentifié.** *Factuel :* l'appel anonyme fonctionne (vérifié). Le code
237	interroge déjà `hub.docker.com` en anonyme pour les dates de tags
238	(`fetchDockerHubTagsMeta`). *Avis :* anonyme. Cela n'envoie aucun secret à un second hôte, et un
239	identifiant périmé ne fait pas échouer la recherche.
240	
241	**Q5, plafonds.** *Factuel :* le délai actuel est de 15 s **par requête** (R3) ;
242	`maxTagPages` = 100. *Avis :*
243	
244	- Hub : `n=50`, une page (plafond serveur à 100) ;
245	- catalogue : `n=1000`, 10 pages au plus, puis « partial » ;
246	- 100 lignes par registre au plus (« partial » au-delà) ;
247	- échéance de 15 s par registre, parcours compris ;
248	- saisie de 2 caractères au moins pour un catalogue, Hub dès 1.
249	
250	**Q6, détail d'un verdict.** *Factuel :* l'en-tête fait 7 lignes sur un quart de la largeur et
251	coupe en silence (R5) ; Rule 139 exclut les lignes factices. *Avis :* le journal seulement, dans
252	le MVP.
253	
254	**Q7, étendue de « limited to cached content ».** *Factuel :* DevDesk ne connaît pas le type
255	(proxy ou hébergé) d'un membre. `GroupMember` et `RegistryGroupMember` ne portent que
256	`Alias, URL, RepoPrefix`. `fetchRepoMeta` lit `type` pour le groupe sans le garder. Le suffixe
257	`-proxy` d'un nom est une convention, et la deviner contredirait « déclaré, jamais deviné ».
258	*Avis :* toute entrée `provider: nexus` de `kind: group` ou membre d'un groupe nexus. Mettre le
259	type du membre en cache est une évolution séparée (détecteur et schéma de cache).
260	
261	**Q8, marqueur « scanned » au niveau 1.** *Factuel :* même obstacle que Q2(B), il faut agréger
262	par dépôt. *Avis :* non dans le MVP, sauf si Q2 est tranchée en (B), auquel cas les deux vont
263	ensemble.
264	
265	**Q9, `←` et `esc` au niveau 1.** *Factuel :* dans l'explorer, les deux remontent d'un niveau
266	(`handleDrillUp`). Au niveau 2 actuel, `←` ne fait rien : la table ignore `left`. *Avis :* oui,
267	les deux ramènent au formulaire. Il est cohérent d'ajouter `←` = `esc` sur les tags atteints par
268	nom exact.
269	
270	**Q10, nom affiché d'une officielle.** *Factuel (vérifié) :* Hub renvoie `nginx`, et
271	`normalizeRepoForRegistry` produit `library/nginx` pour la référence. *Avis :* afficher `nginx`,
272	avec la référence complète dans le pied de la ligne.
273	
274	## Hypothèses retenues (prudentes, sans conséquence sur le verdict)
275	
276	- Hypothèse : la sous-chaîne d'un catalogue se compare à la partie du nom **après** le préfixe
277	  de l'entrée.
278	- Hypothèse : le niveau 1 garde une colonne d'activité, toujours au repos.
279	- Hypothèse : l'adaptateur Hub est choisi par `isDockerHub(url)`, comme le reste du code, et non
280	  par un `provider` nouveau.

20	// browserState tracks which screen the browser is on.
21	type browserState int
22	
23	// browserStateResolving is gone. The browser used to open into it and ignore
24	// every key — esc included — while up to one 8-second detection per configured
25	// registry ran (D13). Members now come from config plus the group cache, so
26	// there is nothing to resolve and the form renders at once, offline included.
27	// browserStateStatus is gone too (§3.60). It was the spinner the browser showed
28	// while a pull ran, and a pull is a job now: the row spins in the Images tab,
29	// which is where asking for one leaves the user.
30	const (
31		browserStateInput browserState = iota // search form
32		browserStateTags                      // results table
33	)
34	
35	// browserRegistryEntry is one selectable registry in the browser form.
36	// Group members have ParentSlug set; standalone registries have it empty.
37	type browserRegistryEntry struct {
38		URL   string
39		Alias string
40		// repoPrefix goes in front of the repository name. With URL it forms the
41		// entry's address, and both the browse path and the pull reference derive
42		// from that one pair — which is what stops them meaning two different
43		// repositories (D39, §3.18).
44		repoPrefix string
45		// Slug identifies the entry: its own for a standalone registry, its group's
46		// for a member. It is what the result filter resolves labels through, and
47		// what replaced matching on URL — two registries configured with the same
48		// URL used to collide.
49		Slug        string
50		ParentAlias string // non-empty = member of a group
51		ParentSlug  string
52		parentURL   string // URL of the parent RegistryItem (for credential lookup)
53		// key identifies the entry among all the others, and is what the checkbox,
54		// the remembered exclusions and every result are keyed on (D40). It is not
55		// the URL: two registries may be declared on one host — the form enforces
56		// slug uniqueness, not URL uniqueness — and §3.18 makes that the ordinary
57		// case, since a member is now a bare host plus a prefix. Nor is it Slug,
58		// which holds the *group's* slug for a member and would give a whole group
59		// one checkbox. So: the slug for a standalone registry, and the group's slug
60		// plus the member's address for a member — the address, not the alias:
61		// cleanMemberAlias strips `-proxy` and `-hosted`, so `docker-io-proxy` and
62		// `docker-io-hosted` both display as `docker-io`.
63		key string
64		// authMode is already resolved: a member carries what its group settled on,
65		// since `inherit` is the only thing the shared credential entry can mean.
66		authMode string
67	}
68	
69	// resultFilter narrows the tag table to one group or one registry. Both empty
70	// means everything.
71	//
72	// The single-registry level is an entry key rather than a URL: several entries
73	// share one host once a member is a host plus a prefix, so a URL would select
74	// every proxy on that instance at once (§3.18, and D40 one screen along).
75	type resultFilter struct {
76		groupSlug string
77		entryKey  string
78	}
79	
80	func (f resultFilter) isEmpty() bool { return f.groupSlug == "" && f.entryKey == "" }
81	
82	// matches reports whether a result from entryKey passes the filter. A group
83	// matches every one of its members, which is what the group level is for.
84	func (f resultFilter) matches(entryKey string, entry *browserRegistryEntry) bool {
85		switch {
86		case f.isEmpty():
87			return true
88		case f.groupSlug != "":
89			return entry != nil && entry.ParentSlug == f.groupSlug
90		default:
91			return entryKey == f.entryKey
92		}
93	}
94	
95	// pickerRow is one line of the registry picker. A group is a row of its own
96	// whose checkbox covers its members, which is the only way to select eight
97	// proxies without eight keystrokes.
98	type pickerRow struct {
99		// groupSlug is set on a group header; entry is -1 there.
100		groupSlug string
101		label     string
102		entry     int // index into b.entries, or -1
103	}
104	
105	// tagRow is one line of the tag table: the tag, plus what the row says about it
106	// that does not live on the tag — the registry's display label, the cached scan
107	// counts, what the activity column says and whether a scan is running.
108	//
109	// The columns are built once, in newRegistryBrowser, so their Cell functions
110	// cannot reach back into the browser for any of that. It is the imageRow
111	// pattern, and it exists for the same reason: a column sorts by the value it
112	// prints.
113	type tagRow struct {
114		tag     MultiRegistryTag
115		label   string // registry alias, or its URL when it has none
116		entry   cache.ImageScanEntry
117		scanned bool
118		// Activity is what the first column and the footer say: a scan or a pull
119		// running, queued or failed, resolved by rebuildTagTable. It carries no
120		// animation phase; the table reads it at render.
121		Activity components.RowActivity
122		// ScanRunning is true while a scan of the tag really runs (not queued): the
123		// severity cells then hold a placeholder instead of the counts.
124		ScanRunning bool
125	}
126	
127	// tagColumns describes the tag results table.
128	func tagColumns() []datatable.Column[tagRow] {
129		return []datatable.Column[tagRow]{
130			// The activity column (Rule 125): untitled, no Less nor Search, empty at rest.
131			datatable.IndicatorColumn(func(r tagRow) indicator.State { return r.Activity.State }, nil, nil),
132			{
133				Title: "Registry", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: 20,
134				Cell: func(r tagRow) string { return r.label },
135			},
136			{
137				Title: "Tag", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: 30, Flex: 1,
138				Cell: func(r tagRow) string { return r.tag.Tag },
139				Less: func(a, b tagRow) bool {
140					return strings.ToLower(a.tag.Tag) < strings.ToLower(b.tag.Tag)
141				},
142			},
143			{
144				Title: "Updated", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, Optional: true, MinWidth: 16,
145				Cell: func(r tagRow) string {
146					if r.tag.UpdatedAt.IsZero() {
147						return "-"
148					}
149					return theme.TimeAgo(r.tag.UpdatedAt)
150				},
151				// Newest first is this column's ascending order: "most recently
152				// updated" is what anyone sorting by it is after.
153				Less: func(a, b tagRow) bool { return a.tag.UpdatedAt.After(b.tag.UpdatedAt) },
154			},
155			tagCVEColumn("C", func(e cache.ImageScanEntry) int { return e.Critical }),
156			tagCVEColumn("H", func(e cache.ImageScanEntry) int { return e.High }),
157			tagCVEColumn("M", func(e cache.ImageScanEntry) int { return e.Medium }),
158			tagCVEColumn("L", func(e cache.ImageScanEntry) int { return e.Low }),
159		}
160	}
161	
162	// tagCVEColumn builds one of the four severity count columns: a dim ellipsis
163	// while a scan runs, the count once one has, and a dash for a tag never scanned —
164	// nought findings and never looked at are different answers. A queued scan or a
165	// pull keeps the counts.
166	func tagCVEColumn(title string, get func(cache.ImageScanEntry) int) datatable.Column[tagRow] {
167		return datatable.Column[tagRow]{
168			Title: title, Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: 4,
169			Cell: func(r tagRow) string {
170				switch {
171				case r.ScanRunning:
172					return "…"
173				case r.scanned:
174					return strconv.Itoa(get(r.entry))
175				default:
176					return "-"
177				}
178			},
179			Style: func(r tagRow) lipgloss.Style {
180				if r.ScanRunning {
181					return theme.DimStyle
182				}
183				return lipgloss.NewStyle()
184			},
185		}
186	}
187	
188	// newTagTable builds the tag table. ActivityTables uses it too, so the guard
189	// sees the real columns even with the browser closed.
190	func newTagTable() *datatable.Model[tagRow] {
191		t := datatable.New(datatable.Config[tagRow]{
192			Columns:    tagColumns(),
193			SortColumn: tagColumnTag,
194		})
195		return &t
196	}
197	
198	const brFieldRepo = 0
199	
200	// brFieldReg returns the form field index for the i-th picker row.
201	func (b *RegistryBrowser) brFieldReg(i int) int { return 1 + i }
202	
203	// brFieldSubmit returns the form field index for the Browse Tags button.
204	func (b *RegistryBrowser) brFieldSubmit() int { return 1 + len(b.rows) }
205	
206	// RegistryBrowserCloseMsg is sent when the user presses ESC on the browser input screen.
207	type RegistryBrowserCloseMsg struct{}
208	
209	// The two sortable columns of the tag table. `.` cycles Tag ascending, Tag
210	// descending, Updated, Updated descending and back — which is what
211	// datatable.CycleSort does over exactly these two, so the cycle is no longer
212	// written out.
213	const (
214		tagColumnTag     = 2
215		tagColumnUpdated = 3
216	)
217	
218	// RegistryBrowser searches image tags across multiple configured registries.
219	type RegistryBrowser struct {
220		registries    []config.RegistryItem
221		width, height int
222	
223		// Entries, built once from config plus the group cache.
224		entries []browserRegistryEntry
225		rows    []pickerRow
226	
227		// Form state
228		repoInput    textinput.Model
229		selectedRegs map[string]bool // entry key → checked
230		focusedField int
231	
232		// Results state
233		tags            []MultiRegistryTag
234		pendingSearches int
235		registryFilter  resultFilter
236		tagTable        datatable.Model[tagRow]
237		scanCache       map[string]cache.ImageScanEntry
238	
239		// The router's snapshot, for the activity column and the footer: the
240		// registry's runs and remembered failures, and the context they are read in.
241		jobs        []jobs.Run
242		failures    []jobs.Failure
243		contextName string
244	
245		// Tag filter in the results view. The sort belongs to the table now; this
246		// filter stays here because it narrows the tags before the table sees them,
247		// alongside registryFilter, and because it is drawn in the OCI view's own
248		// footer rather than the table's bar.
249		filterInput  textinput.Model
250		filterActive bool
251	
252		state browserState
253	}
254	
255	// newRegistryBrowser creates a RegistryBrowser showing its form immediately.
256	//
257	// A group's members come from the cache the Registries tab refreshes, so
258	// opening the browser reads a file rather than the network — which is what
259	// removed the resolving state D13 is about, rather than papering over it.
260	func newRegistryBrowser(
261		registries []config.RegistryItem,
262		groups map[string]cache.RegistryGroupEntry,
263		deselected map[string]bool,
264		width, height int,
265	) *RegistryBrowser {
266		repoInput := textinput.New()
267		repoInput.Placeholder = "nginx  (or library/nginx)"
268		repoInput.CharLimit = 256
269		theme.StyleTextInput(&repoInput)
270		repoInput.Focus()
271	
272		fi := textinput.New()
273		fi.Placeholder = "filter tags…"
274		fi.CharLimit = 128
275		theme.StyleTextInput(&fi)
276	
277		b := &RegistryBrowser{
278			registries:   registries,
279			width:        width,
280			height:       height,
281			repoInput:    repoInput,
282			selectedRegs: make(map[string]bool),
283			focusedField: brFieldRepo,
284			filterInput:  fi,
285			tagTable:     *newTagTable(),
286			scanCache:    make(map[string]cache.ImageScanEntry),
287			state:        browserStateInput,
288		}
289		b.buildEntries(groups, deselected)
290		b.resizeInputs()
291		b.resizeTagTable()
292		b.updateFocus()
293		return b
294	}
295	
296	// buildEntries expands every configured registry into the lines the picker
297	// shows: a group into its cached members under a header, anything else into
298	// itself.
299	//
300	// A selection is remembered as the entries that were *un*checked, so a member
301	// discovered since the last visit arrives checked like every other new one.
302	func (b *RegistryBrowser) buildEntries(groups map[string]cache.RegistryGroupEntry, deselected map[string]bool) {
303		b.entries = nil
304		b.rows = nil
305		for _, reg := range b.registries {
306			alias := browserAlias(reg)
307			// Members share their group's host and therefore its single credential
308			// entry, so they share the decision the group made about using it.
309			mode := config.ResolveAuthMode(reg, nil)
310	
311			members := groups[reg.Slug].Members
312			if reg.Kind != config.KindGroup || len(members) == 0 {
313				// A group nobody has discovered yet is offered as itself: it is a
314				// pullable registry too, and hiding it would be worse than listing
315				// it without the members it may have.
316				b.rows = append(b.rows, pickerRow{label: alias, entry: len(b.entries)})
317				b.entries = append(b.entries, browserRegistryEntry{
318					URL: reg.URL, Alias: alias, Slug: reg.Slug, authMode: mode,
319					repoPrefix: reg.RepoPrefix,
320					key:        reg.Slug,
321				})
322				continue
323			}
324	
325			b.rows = append(b.rows, pickerRow{groupSlug: reg.Slug, label: alias, entry: -1})
326			for _, m := range members {
327				b.rows = append(b.rows, pickerRow{label: "  " + m.Alias, entry: len(b.entries)})
328				b.entries = append(b.entries, browserRegistryEntry{
329					URL:         m.URL,
330					Alias:       m.Alias,
331					repoPrefix:  m.RepoPrefix,
332					Slug:        reg.Slug,
333					ParentAlias: alias,
334					ParentSlug:  reg.Slug,
335					parentURL:   reg.URL,
336					authMode:    mode,
337					key:         memberKey(reg.Slug, m.URL, m.RepoPrefix),
338				})
339			}
340		}
341	
342		b.selectedRegs = make(map[string]bool, len(b.entries))
343		for _, e := range b.entries {
344			b.selectedRegs[e.key] = !deselected[e.key]
345		}
346	}
347	
348	// memberKey names one member of a group. Scoping it by the group's slug is what
349	// keeps two groups fronting the same repository apart, and what keeps a member
350	// from colliding with a standalone registry keyed on its own slug.
351	//
352	// The URL alone will not do: every member of a path-routed group answers to the
353	// same host now, and the prefix is the whole of what tells them apart (§3.18).
354	func memberKey(groupSlug, memberURL, repoPrefix string) string {
355		return groupSlug + "/" + memberURL + "/" + repoPrefix
356	}
357	
358	// browserAlias returns what a registry is labelled with in the browser.
359	//
360	// With no alias it falls back to the entry's *address* rather than its URL: one
361	// line per proxy is one host repeated, so the URL alone would label every proxy
362	// of an instance identically (§3.18).
363	func browserAlias(reg config.RegistryItem) string {
364		if reg.Alias != "" {
365			return reg.Alias
366		}
367		return registryRef(reg.URL, reg.RepoPrefix)
368	}
369	
370	// selected reports whether an entry is checked.
371	func (b *RegistryBrowser) selected(e browserRegistryEntry) bool { return b.selectedRegs[e.key] }
372	
373	// groupState reports whether all, none or some of a group's members are checked.
374	func (b *RegistryBrowser) groupState(slug string) theme.CheckState {
375		checked, total := 0, 0
376		for _, e := range b.entries {
377			if e.ParentSlug != slug {
378				continue
379			}
380			total++
381			if b.selected(e) {
382				checked++
383			}
384		}
385		switch {
386		case total == 0 || checked == 0:
387			return theme.CheckNone
388		case checked == total:
389			return theme.CheckAll
390		default:
391			return theme.CheckSome
392		}
393	}
394	
395	// toggleGroup checks every member of a group, or unchecks them when they were
396	// all already checked. A partial selection resolves upwards: the user is more
397	// likely to be completing it than discarding it.
398	func (b *RegistryBrowser) toggleGroup(slug string) {
399		want := b.groupState(slug) != theme.CheckAll
400		for _, e := range b.entries {
401			if e.ParentSlug == slug {
402				b.selectedRegs[e.key] = want
403			}
404		}
405	}
406	
407	// Deselected returns the keys of the entries the user unchecked, which is what
408	// is remembered between visits.
409	func (b *RegistryBrowser) Deselected() []string {
410		var out []string
411		for _, e := range b.entries {
412			if !b.selected(e) {
413				out = append(out, e.key)
414			}
415		}
416		return out
417	}
418	
419	// SetSize updates dimensions and resizes internal components.
420	func (b *RegistryBrowser) SetSize(width, height int) {
421		b.width = width
422		b.height = height
423		b.resizeInputs()
424		b.resizeTagTable()
425	}
426	
427	func (b *RegistryBrowser) resizeInputs() {
428		w := max(b.width-22, 20)
429		b.repoInput.SetWidth(w)
430		b.filterInput.SetWidth(max(b.width-6, 10))
431	}
432	
433	// resizeTagTable hands the table the viewport width.
434	//
435	// b.width is already the content width — the caller subtracted the borders —
436	// and datatable.Resize subtracts them itself, so they are added back here. The
437	// column solving, the Rule 116 remainder and the selected row's width are all
438	// its business now.
439	func (b *RegistryBrowser) resizeTagTable() {
440		b.tagTable.Resize(b.width+2, max(b.height, 1))
441	}
442

## Code editing instructions

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function
- **Naming**: `handle[MessageType]` (e.g. `handleContextSwitch()`, `handleKeyPress()`)
- **Pattern**: The function must return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

**Before (bad):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    return a.handleContextSwitch(msg)

// Further down in the file
func (a *App) handleContextSwitch(msg ContextSwitchCompleteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
}
```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

#### Error handling
- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

#### Comments
- **Mandatory for**:
  - Exported (public) functions
  - Complex business logic
  - Workarounds or non-obvious decisions
- **Format**: `// functionName does X and returns Y`
- **Avoid**: Comments that repeat the code

#### Complexity
- **Maximum 3 levels of indentation** in a function
- **Functions > 50 lines**: refactor into smaller functions
- **Switch > 10 cases**: consider a table-driven pattern

## Code quality rules and proactive checks

### Rule 301 : Systematic code quality check before commit

**MANDATORY**: Before creating a commit, ALWAYS perform the following checks:

#### 1. Go linter (golangci-lint)
```bash
golangci-lint run
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix ALL warnings and errors
- ✅ Specifically check deprecation warnings (SA1019)
- ✅ NEVER ignore warnings without documented justification

#### 2. Tests
```bash
go test ./...
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that all tests pass
- ✅ If tests fail, fix them BEFORE the commit

#### 3. Build
```bash
go build
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that the build succeeds without errors
- ✅ Test the application if functional changes were made

#### 4. Deprecated dependencies

**Detection:**
- Check golangci-lint SA1019 warnings
- Look in go.mod for packages marked as deprecated

**Action:**
- Replace IMMEDIATELY with a maintained alternative
- Document the replacement in the commit message
- Update the documentation (.claude/CLAUDE.md)

**Examples of common replacements:**
- `github.com/go-ping/ping` → `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing`

### Rule 302 : IDE diagnostics check

**MANDATORY**: Before each commit, check the IDE diagnostics:

```
Use mcp__ide__getDiagnostics to check:
- Compilation errors
- Unused parameters
- Unused imports
- Other warnings
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix or justify every diagnostic
- ✅ Do not ignore "unused parameter" without a reason

### Rule 303 : go.mod and dependencies

# TUI — Forms & Focus

### Rule 103 : Standardized form navigation

- `↑ / ↓` to navigate between a form's fields
- A visual indicator (`theme.IconCircleSmall`) must show the focused element
- `Enter` to validate action buttons only (see Rule 135)

### Rule 104 : Modal window structure

- Rounded border (NormalBorder) with color appropriate to the context
- Title at the top using `theme.TitleStyle`
- Message in the center
- Buttons at the bottom with consistent spacing
- Help instructions with `theme.HelpStyle` at the very bottom
- Safe choice by default (e.g. "No" for delete confirmations)

**Palette variant (selector, Rule 112).** Border and title only: the title sits in
the top border, the border is `theme.ColorPaletteBorder`, there are no buttons and
no help line (Rule 134; the header lists the keys). Every line has an explicit
background and the exact width of the frame.

### Rule 113 : Form field spacing

| Layout | Separator after the field |
|--------|--------------------------|
| **Multi-line**: label ↵ content | `\n\n` (blank line) |
| **Single-line**: label + content on the same line | `\n` |
| **Checkboxes** | `\n` between them, `\n\n` after the group |

`renderField()` functions must **NOT** include the trailing separator.

### Rule 114 : Built-in help system (`?`)

**Every view implements `help.Provider` via `GetHelpContent()`, always in English.**

Obligations:
- Mandatory update in the same commit whenever a feature / keybinding changes
- Every new view must implement `help.Provider` with complete content

Expected content: `Title`, `Description`, `KeyBindings`, `Sections`

Files:
- `internal/ui/help/help.go` — component and `Provider` interface
- `internal/ui/*/view.go` or `model.go` — per-view implementation

**Declared gap: the command palette has no in-app help.** It is not a view; its
keys (`↑↓`, `tab`, `enter`, `esc`) are in the header while it is open and
documented in `docs-site/docs/reference/commands.md` (DEVDESK-89, decision of
the user).

### Rule 120 : Focus indicator and form field rendering

**Indentation: 2 characters.** When focused, `theme.IconCircleSmall` sits at column 0.

| State | Prefix |
|------|---------|
| Focused | `IconCircleSmall + " "` → `● Label` |
| Not focused | `"  "` (2 spaces) → `  Label` |

`theme.IconCircleSmall` (`\ueb8a`) does NOT contain a space — always add `" "` after it.

**Label/value separator**: `theme.IconChevronRight` (`\uf054`) + `" "`. **No `:`**.

**A space before the chevron is mandatory**: there must always be a space between the label text and `IconChevronRight`.

```go
// ✅ Single-line, focused
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Server " + theme.IconChevronRight + " ") + input.View()

// ✅ Multi-ligne
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Name " + theme.IconChevronRight) + "\n"
theme.Bg("  ") + input.View()

// ❌ WRONG — no space before the chevron
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Name" + theme.IconChevronRight) + "\n"
theme.KeyStyle.Render("▸ Server: ") + input.View()
```

**Selection lists**: `IconCircleSmall` for the selected item, `"  "` for the others.

**Focus color**: `theme.ColorHighlight` for all field types.

**TextInput cursor**: configure via `theme.StyleTextInput(&myInput)` (sets `Prompt = ""`).

**Checkboxes**: via `theme.RenderCheckbox()`.

**There are no radio buttons.** For a closed set of values, the control is
the `←→` cycle field (Rule 132) — regardless of how many values there are,
even two. `theme.RenderRadioButton()` was removed along with its last two
callers (§3.9 of the backlog); recreating it locally is forbidden.

Forbidden:
- ❌ `▸` as a focus indicator (use `theme.IconCircleSmall`)
- ❌ `:` as the label/value separator (use `theme.IconChevronRight`)
- ❌ `ColorPrimary` for focused elements (use `ColorHighlight`)
- ❌ Recreating `RenderCheckbox` locally
- ❌ Reintroducing radio buttons, in any form

### Rule 131 : Top padding for forms in the viewport

**Every form displayed in the main viewport must begin with exactly one blank line (1-line top padding).**

```go
// ✅ CORRECT — a single blank line
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n" +
        f.renderFields()
}

// ❌ WRONG — two blank lines (EmptyLineBg + "\n\n")
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n\n" + f.renderFields()
}

// ❌ WRONG — form stuck to the viewport's top edge
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return f.renderFields()
}
```

Does not apply to modals (positioned via `lipgloss.Place`).

### Rule 132 : Closed-list fields (value cycling)

**Any field whose value belongs to a finite set must use the ←→ cycle pattern.**

It is the **only** control allowed for a closed set. Radio buttons are not
an alternative for two or three values: they no longer exist in the
application (Rule 120). Checkboxes remain for independent booleans, which is
a different thing from an exclusive choice.

#### Visual

```
  Visibility  󰅂 private        ← not focused
● Visibility  󰅂 internal       ← focused (KeyStyle)
```

Line structure:

| Part | Value |
|--------|--------|
| Focus indicator | `theme.IconCircleSmall + " "` (focused) or `"  "` (not focused) |
| Label | field text, e.g. `"Visibility"` |
| Selection icon | `" " + theme.IconSelect + " "` |
| Separator | `theme.IconChevronRight + " "` |
| Current value | plain text with `ColorText` |

#### Navigation

- `←` / `→`: move to the previous / next value (cycling)
- `Tab` / `Shift+Tab`: navigate to the previous / next field

Do not use `Enter` to cycle — `Enter` confirms the form or advances to the next field.

#### Reference implementation

```go
// Rendu
func (f *Form) renderCycleField(label string, options []string, idx int, fieldIdx int) string {
    selectLabel := label + " " + theme.IconSelect + " "
    value := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorText).Render(options[idx])
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        return theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall+" "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
    }
    return theme.Bg("  "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
}

// Key handling
case "left":
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        f.idx = (f.idx - 1 + len(f.options)) % len(f.options)
    }
case "right":
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        f.idx = (f.idx + 1) % len(f.options)
    }
```

Forbidden:
- ❌ Using `Enter` to cycle values
- ❌ Opening a dropdown list for 2–4 values (reserve that for long lists, cf. `renderTemplateList`)
- ❌ Hardcoding the value's color (use `ColorText`)
- ❌ Using radio buttons for a closed set (Rule 120)

### Rule 121 : Circular iconography for statuses

Status indicators in tables and lists must use circular icons:

| State | Icon |
|------|-------|
| Success / OK | `theme.IconOK` (`\uf058`) |
| Error / Failure | `theme.IconError` (`\uf057`) |
| Warning | `theme.IconWarning` (`\uf071`) |

Applies to: scan results, pipeline statuses, UP/DOWN indicators.
Does not apply to: object-type icons (folders, files, GitLab logo).

**Amendment (DEVDESK-137): the activity column is not covered.** In the activity
column (Rule 125, "The activity column"), the state is a glyph of
`internal/ui/indicator` (`● ○ ◴ ⊗ ◐ ◕ ◉ ⊘ ⊖ ◌`), colored by the closed
`theme.ColorActivity*` aliases, and not `IconOK` / `IconError` / `IconWarning`.
Every other status column (Verdict, Update, Sig, scan results, UP/DOWN) keeps
the three icons above, unchanged.

### Rule 133 : Multi-line text fields — `WrappedInput` mandatory

**`bubbles/textarea` is forbidden.** Its internal background is not controllable by lipgloss and produces visual artifacts (a `┃` gutter, terminal background between lines).

Use **`components.WrappedInput`** (`internal/ui/components/wrapped_input.go`) for any text field that must display across multiple lines.

#### API

```go
// Creation
field := components.NewWrappedInput(wrapWidth, charLimit, "placeholder text")

// Resizing — call inside the tea.WindowSizeMsg handler
field.SetDisplayWidth(terminalWidth)

// Focus / Blur
field.Focus()   // called from updateFocus()
field.Blur()    // called from updateFocus()

// Dans Update() — passer les messages clavier quand le champ a le focus
field, cmd = field.Update(msg)

// In View() — returns the multi-line content block, ready to concatenate
return labelStr + "\n" + field.View()

// Retrieving the value on submit
value := field.Value()
```

#### `wrapWidth` parameter

`wrapWidth` is the number of **runes** per visual line before wrapping (word-wrap at the last space, hard-break if there is no space).

| Context | Recommended value |
|----------|--------------------|
| GitLab description (group/project) | `80` |
| Short notes field | `60` |
| Long text field | `100` |

```go
// ✅ CORRECT
const descWrapWidth = 80
descInput := components.NewWrappedInput(descWrapWidth, 250, "description (optional)")

// ❌ WRONG
descInput := textarea.New()
```

#### Behavior

- Empty field + focused → only the block cursor is shown
- Empty field + not focused → placeholder in `ColorDim`
- Filled field → word-wrapped text, each line padded with `theme.PadWithBg` up to `displayWidth`
- Inverted block cursor (`ColorText` bg / `ColorBackground` fg) at the exact caret position

Forbidden:
- ❌ `bubbles/textarea` in any view
- ❌ Recreating the word-wrap or cursor logic locally
- ❌ Forgetting to call `SetDisplayWidth` in the `tea.WindowSizeMsg` handler

### Rule 135 : Strict keybinding assignment in forms ⚠️

**Every key has a single, unambiguous role.** These rules apply to every form in the application without exception.

| Key | Exclusive role |
|--------|---------------|
| `↑ / ↓` | Navigate between a form's fields |
| `Tab / Shift+Tab` | Switch between tabs **only** — never for navigation between fields |
| `Space` | Toggle a checkbox — the **only** key allowed for this role |
| `Enter` | Validate an action button or trigger a specific action — **never** to toggle a checkbox |
| `← / →` | Change level in a table (drill-down/up) **and** cycle the values of a closed-list field |
| `Esc` | Cancel / close / return to the parent level |

**Declared exception: the command line.** `tab` completes the highlighted
suggestion there (`keymap.DeclaredExceptions()`, surface `app/command-line`). The
command line has no tabs and no fields, so neither job of `tab` exists on it.

#### Detailed rules

**`Tab / Shift+Tab` — tabs only**
- Reserved for switching between tabs (`bubbles/table` breadcrumb, result tabs, etc.)
- Must **never** be used to move forward/backward between form fields
- If a view has no tabs, `Tab` must do nothing (or be ignored)

**`↑ / ↓` — navigation between fields**
- The only keys to move focus from one field to another in a form
- In a list/table outside a form: row-by-row movement (Rule 111)

**`Space` — toggle checkbox**
- The only valid key to check/uncheck a checkbox
- Match it as `keymap.Space`, never as a `" "` literal (Bubble Tea v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`; `keymap.Space` is `"space"`); `TestNoKeyIsComparedToALiteralSpace` fails on a literal
- Reference implementation: `LaunchForm` (`internal/ui/oci_resources`), pinned by `launch_form_keys_test.go` — `TestLaunchFormSpaceTogglesEachCheckbox`, `TestLaunchFormDetachAndInteractiveExcludeEachOther`, `TestLaunchFormEnterNeverTogglesACheckbox`
- `Enter` on a checkbox must be ignored or advance to the next field, never toggle it
- **Confirmation buttons are the mirror case**: `Space` never answers Yes or No. `components.ConfirmModal`, `ChoiceModal`, `OptionConfirmModal` and the setup wizard's confirmation answer on `enter` only (plus `y`/`n` on the yes/no ones). In `OptionConfirmModal`, `space` toggles the option checkbox when it has focus (inert when locked) and `enter` on that checkbox is ignored

// ✅ CORRECT — Space to toggle

        m.myCheckbox = !m.myCheckbox
    }

// ✅ CORRECT — ↑/↓ to navigate between fields

    m.focusedField = max(m.focusedField-1, 0)

# TUI — Forms & Focus

### Rule 103 : Standardized form navigation

- `↑ / ↓` to navigate between a form's fields
- A visual indicator (`theme.IconCircleSmall`) must show the focused element
- `Enter` to validate action buttons only (see Rule 135)

### Rule 104 : Modal window structure

- Rounded border (NormalBorder) with color appropriate to the context
- Title at the top using `theme.TitleStyle`
- Message in the center
- Buttons at the bottom with consistent spacing
- Help instructions with `theme.HelpStyle` at the very bottom
- Safe choice by default (e.g. "No" for delete confirmations)

**Palette variant (selector, Rule 112).** Border and title only: the title sits in
the top border, the border is `theme.ColorPaletteBorder`, there are no buttons and
no help line (Rule 134; the header lists the keys). Every line has an explicit
background and the exact width of the frame.

### Rule 113 : Form field spacing

| Layout | Separator after the field |
|--------|--------------------------|
| **Multi-line**: label ↵ content | `\n\n` (blank line) |
| **Single-line**: label + content on the same line | `\n` |
| **Checkboxes** | `\n` between them, `\n\n` after the group |

`renderField()` functions must **NOT** include the trailing separator.

### Rule 114 : Built-in help system (`?`)

**Every view implements `help.Provider` via `GetHelpContent()`, always in English.**

Obligations:
- Mandatory update in the same commit whenever a feature / keybinding changes
- Every new view must implement `help.Provider` with complete content

Expected content: `Title`, `Description`, `KeyBindings`, `Sections`

Files:
- `internal/ui/help/help.go` — component and `Provider` interface
- `internal/ui/*/view.go` or `model.go` — per-view implementation

**Declared gap: the command palette has no in-app help.** It is not a view; its
keys (`↑↓`, `tab`, `enter`, `esc`) are in the header while it is open and
documented in `docs-site/docs/reference/commands.md` (DEVDESK-89, decision of
the user).

### Rule 120 : Focus indicator and form field rendering

**Indentation: 2 characters.** When focused, `theme.IconCircleSmall` sits at column 0.

| State | Prefix |
|------|---------|
| Focused | `IconCircleSmall + " "` → `● Label` |
| Not focused | `"  "` (2 spaces) → `  Label` |

`theme.IconCircleSmall` (`\ueb8a`) does NOT contain a space — always add `" "` after it.

**Label/value separator**: `theme.IconChevronRight` (`\uf054`) + `" "`. **No `:`**.

**A space before the chevron is mandatory**: there must always be a space between the label text and `IconChevronRight`.

```go
// ✅ Single-line, focused
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Server " + theme.IconChevronRight + " ") + input.View()

// ✅ Multi-ligne
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Name " + theme.IconChevronRight) + "\n"
theme.Bg("  ") + input.View()

// ❌ WRONG — no space before the chevron
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Name" + theme.IconChevronRight) + "\n"
theme.KeyStyle.Render("▸ Server: ") + input.View()
```

**Selection lists**: `IconCircleSmall` for the selected item, `"  "` for the others.

**Focus color**: `theme.ColorHighlight` for all field types.

**TextInput cursor**: configure via `theme.StyleTextInput(&myInput)` (sets `Prompt = ""`).

**Checkboxes**: via `theme.RenderCheckbox()`.

**There are no radio buttons.** For a closed set of values, the control is
the `←→` cycle field (Rule 132) — regardless of how many values there are,
even two. `theme.RenderRadioButton()` was removed along with its last two
callers (§3.9 of the backlog); recreating it locally is forbidden.

Forbidden:
- ❌ `▸` as a focus indicator (use `theme.IconCircleSmall`)
- ❌ `:` as the label/value separator (use `theme.IconChevronRight`)
- ❌ `ColorPrimary` for focused elements (use `ColorHighlight`)
- ❌ Recreating `RenderCheckbox` locally
- ❌ Reintroducing radio buttons, in any form

### Rule 131 : Top padding for forms in the viewport

**Every form displayed in the main viewport must begin with exactly one blank line (1-line top padding).**

```go
// ✅ CORRECT — a single blank line
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n" +
        f.renderFields()
}

// ❌ WRONG — two blank lines (EmptyLineBg + "\n\n")
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n\n" + f.renderFields()
}

// ❌ WRONG — form stuck to the viewport's top edge
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return f.renderFields()
}
```

Does not apply to modals (positioned via `lipgloss.Place`).

### Rule 132 : Closed-list fields (value cycling)

**Any field whose value belongs to a finite set must use the ←→ cycle pattern.**

It is the **only** control allowed for a closed set. Radio buttons are not
an alternative for two or three values: they no longer exist in the
application (Rule 120). Checkboxes remain for independent booleans, which is
a different thing from an exclusive choice.

#### Visual

```
  Visibility  󰅂 private        ← not focused
● Visibility  󰅂 internal       ← focused (KeyStyle)
```

Line structure:

| Part | Value |
|--------|--------|
| Focus indicator | `theme.IconCircleSmall + " "` (focused) or `"  "` (not focused) |
| Label | field text, e.g. `"Visibility"` |
| Selection icon | `" " + theme.IconSelect + " "` |
| Separator | `theme.IconChevronRight + " "` |
| Current value | plain text with `ColorText` |

#### Navigation

- `←` / `→`: move to the previous / next value (cycling)
- `Tab` / `Shift+Tab`: navigate to the previous / next field

Do not use `Enter` to cycle — `Enter` confirms the form or advances to the next field.

#### Reference implementation

```go
// Rendu
func (f *Form) renderCycleField(label string, options []string, idx int, fieldIdx int) string {
    selectLabel := label + " " + theme.IconSelect + " "
    value := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorText).Render(options[idx])
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        return theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall+" "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
    }
    return theme.Bg("  "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
}

// Key handling
case "left":
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        f.idx = (f.idx - 1 + len(f.options)) % len(f.options)
    }
case "right":
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        f.idx = (f.idx + 1) % len(f.options)
    }
```

Forbidden:
- ❌ Using `Enter` to cycle values
- ❌ Opening a dropdown list for 2–4 values (reserve that for long lists, cf. `renderTemplateList`)
- ❌ Hardcoding the value's color (use `ColorText`)
- ❌ Using radio buttons for a closed set (Rule 120)

### Rule 121 : Circular iconography for statuses

Status indicators in tables and lists must use circular icons:

| State | Icon |
|------|-------|
| Success / OK | `theme.IconOK` (`\uf058`) |
| Error / Failure | `theme.IconError` (`\uf057`) |
| Warning | `theme.IconWarning` (`\uf071`) |

Applies to: scan results, pipeline statuses, UP/DOWN indicators.
Does not apply to: object-type icons (folders, files, GitLab logo).

**Amendment (DEVDESK-137): the activity column is not covered.** In the activity
column (Rule 125, "The activity column"), the state is a glyph of
`internal/ui/indicator` (`● ○ ◴ ⊗ ◐ ◕ ◉ ⊘ ⊖ ◌`), colored by the closed
`theme.ColorActivity*` aliases, and not `IconOK` / `IconError` / `IconWarning`.
Every other status column (Verdict, Update, Sig, scan results, UP/DOWN) keeps
the three icons above, unchanged.

### Rule 133 : Multi-line text fields — `WrappedInput` mandatory

**`bubbles/textarea` is forbidden.** Its internal background is not controllable by lipgloss and produces visual artifacts (a `┃` gutter, terminal background between lines).

Use **`components.WrappedInput`** (`internal/ui/components/wrapped_input.go`) for any text field that must display across multiple lines.

#### API

```go
// Creation
field := components.NewWrappedInput(wrapWidth, charLimit, "placeholder text")

// Resizing — call inside the tea.WindowSizeMsg handler
field.SetDisplayWidth(terminalWidth)

// Focus / Blur
field.Focus()   // called from updateFocus()
field.Blur()    // called from updateFocus()

// Dans Update() — passer les messages clavier quand le champ a le focus
field, cmd = field.Update(msg)

// In View() — returns the multi-line content block, ready to concatenate
return labelStr + "\n" + field.View()

// Retrieving the value on submit
value := field.Value()
```

#### `wrapWidth` parameter

`wrapWidth` is the number of **runes** per visual line before wrapping (word-wrap at the last space, hard-break if there is no space).

| Context | Recommended value |
|----------|--------------------|
| GitLab description (group/project) | `80` |
| Short notes field | `60` |
| Long text field | `100` |

```go
// ✅ CORRECT
const descWrapWidth = 80
descInput := components.NewWrappedInput(descWrapWidth, 250, "description (optional)")

// ❌ WRONG
descInput := textarea.New()
```

#### Behavior

- Empty field + focused → only the block cursor is shown
- Empty field + not focused → placeholder in `ColorDim`
- Filled field → word-wrapped text, each line padded with `theme.PadWithBg` up to `displayWidth`
- Inverted block cursor (`ColorText` bg / `ColorBackground` fg) at the exact caret position

Forbidden:
- ❌ `bubbles/textarea` in any view
- ❌ Recreating the word-wrap or cursor logic locally
- ❌ Forgetting to call `SetDisplayWidth` in the `tea.WindowSizeMsg` handler

### Rule 135 : Strict keybinding assignment in forms ⚠️

**Every key has a single, unambiguous role.** These rules apply to every form in the application without exception.

| Key | Exclusive role |
|--------|---------------|
| `↑ / ↓` | Navigate between a form's fields |
| `Tab / Shift+Tab` | Switch between tabs **only** — never for navigation between fields |
| `Space` | Toggle a checkbox — the **only** key allowed for this role |
| `Enter` | Validate an action button or trigger a specific action — **never** to toggle a checkbox |
| `← / →` | Change level in a table (drill-down/up) **and** cycle the values of a closed-list field |
| `Esc` | Cancel / close / return to the parent level |

**Declared exception: the command line.** `tab` completes the highlighted
suggestion there (`keymap.DeclaredExceptions()`, surface `app/command-line`). The
command line has no tabs and no fields, so neither job of `tab` exists on it.

**`Tab / Shift+Tab` — tabs only**
- Reserved for switching between tabs (`bubbles/table` breadcrumb, result tabs, etc.)
- Must **never** be used to move forward/backward between form fields
- If a view has no tabs, `Tab` must do nothing (or be ignored)

**`↑ / ↓` — navigation between fields**
- The only keys to move focus from one field to another in a form
- In a list/table outside a form: row-by-row movement (Rule 111)

**`Space` — toggle checkbox**

- Match it as `keymap.Space`, never as a `" "` literal (Bubble Tea v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`; `keymap.Space` is `"space"`); `TestNoKeyIsComparedToALiteralSpace` fails on a literal

In `OptionConfirmModal`, `space` toggles the option checkbox when it has focus (inert when locked) and `enter` on that checkbox is ignored

**`Enter` — validation / action**
- Validates the currently focused button
- Triggers a contextual action (e.g. launch a scan, open a detail view)
- Must **not** toggle a checkbox

**`← / →` — table navigation and value cycling**
- In a table: `←` moves up a level (drill up), `→` moves down a level (drill down)
- On a closed-list field (cycle field): `←` previous value, `→` next value (Rule 132)
- Must **not** move focus between form fields

#### Common violations to avoid

```go

    m.focusedField = (m.focusedField + 1) % fieldCount

// ❌ WRONG — Enter to toggle a checkbox
case "enter":
    if m.focusedField == fieldMyCheckbox {
        m.myCheckbox = !m.myCheckbox
    }

// ✅ CORRECT — Space to toggle
case keymap.Space:
    if m.focusedField == fieldMyCheckbox {
        m.myCheckbox = !m.myCheckbox
    }

// ✅ CORRECT — ↑/↓ to navigate between fields
case "up":
    m.focusedField = max(m.focusedField-1, 0)
case "down":
    m.focusedField = min(m.focusedField+1, fieldCount-1)
```

### Rule 140 : An invalid field is underlined, and the footer says why (DEVDESK-292)

**A field that fails validation gets a wavy red underline, and the same error is in the footer. The underline is never the only carrier.**

- **One entry point.** The underline comes from `theme.StyleInvalidField(base)` (curly underline, `UnderlineCurly`, colour `theme.ColorInvalidField`). - **Prefix unchanged.** The focus prefix `●` stays as in Rule 120. The underline adds no cell: the rendered width does not change.
- **Fallback.** A terminal without styled underlines gets a plain underline (SGR 4), still readable. Cost: about 60 bytes per underlined character. Risk: SGR 58 and `4:3` on old terminals, to check by hand.

```go

f.marks.Sync(keyName, &f.nameInput, f.validation.Invalid(keyName))

// ❌ WRONG — a local underline, and a restyle on every message

```

        return theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall+" "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
    }
    return theme.Bg("  "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
}

case "left":
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        f.idx = (f.idx - 1 + len(f.options)) % len(f.options)
    }
case "right":

    }
```

Forbidden:
- ❌ Using `Enter` to cycle values
- ❌ Opening a dropdown list for 2–4 values (reserve that for long lists, cf. `renderTemplateList`)
- ❌ Hardcoding the value's color (use `ColorText`)
- ❌ Using radio buttons for a closed set (Rule 120)

### Rule 121 : Circular iconography for statuses

Status indicators in tables and lists must use circular icons:

| State | Icon |
|------|-------|
| Success / OK | `theme.IconOK` (`\uf058`) |
| Error / Failure | `theme.IconError` (`\uf057`) |
| Warning | `theme.IconWarning` (`\uf071`) |

Applies to: scan results, pipeline statuses, UP/DOWN indicators.
Does not apply to: object-type icons (folders, files, GitLab logo).

column (Rule 125, "The activity column"), the state is a glyph of
`internal/ui/indicator` (`● ○ ◴ ⊗ ◐ ◕ ◉ ⊘ ⊖ ◌`), colored by the closed

**`bubbles/textarea` is forbidden.** Its internal background is not controllable by lipgloss and produces visual artifacts (a `┃` gutter, terminal background between lines).

#### API

```go
// Creation
field := components.NewWrappedInput(wrapWidth, charLimit, "placeholder text")

// Resizing — call inside the tea.WindowSizeMsg handler
field.SetDisplayWidth(terminalWidth)

// Focus / Blur
field.Focus()   // called from updateFocus()
field.Blur()    // called from updateFocus()

// Dans Update() — passer les messages clavier quand le champ a le focus
field, cmd = field.Update(msg)

// In View() — returns the multi-line content block, ready to concatenate
return labelStr + "\n" + field.View()

// Retrieving the value on submit
value := field.Value()
```

#### `wrapWidth` parameter

`wrapWidth` is the number of **runes** per visual line before wrapping (word-wrap at the last space, hard-break if there is no space).

| Context | Recommended value |
|----------|--------------------|
| GitLab description (group/project) | `80` |
| Short notes field | `60` |
| Long text field | `100` |

```go
// ✅ CORRECT
const descWrapWidth = 80
descInput := components.NewWrappedInput(descWrapWidth, 250, "description (optional)")

// ❌ WRONG
descInput := textarea.New()
```

#### Behavior

- Empty field + focused → only the block cursor is shown
- Empty field + not focused → placeholder in `ColorDim`
- Filled field → word-wrapped text, each line padded with `theme.PadWithBg` up to `displayWidth`
- Inverted block cursor (`ColorText` bg / `ColorBackground` fg) at the exact caret position

Forbidden:
- ❌ `bubbles/textarea` in any view
- ❌ Recreating the word-wrap or cursor logic locally
- ❌ Forgetting to call `SetDisplayWidth` in the `tea.WindowSizeMsg` handler

### Rule 135 : Strict keybinding assignment in forms ⚠️

**Every key has a single, unambiguous role.** These rules apply to every form in the application without exception.

| Key | Exclusive role |
|--------|---------------|
| `↑ / ↓` | Navigate between a form's fields |
| `Tab / Shift+Tab` | Switch between tabs **only** — never for navigation between fields |
| `Space` | Toggle a checkbox — the **only** key allowed for this role |
| `Enter` | Validate an action button or trigger a specific action — **never** to toggle a checkbox |
| `← / →` | Change level in a table (drill-down/up) **and** cycle the values of a closed-list field |
| `Esc` | Cancel / close / return to the parent level |

**Declared exception: the command line.** `tab` completes the highlighted
suggestion there (`keymap.DeclaredExceptions()`, surface `app/command-line`). The
command line has no tabs and no fields, so neither job of `tab` exists on it.

#### Detailed rules

**`Tab / Shift+Tab` — tabs only**
- Reserved for switching between tabs (`bubbles/table` breadcrumb, result tabs, etc.)
- Must **never** be used to move forward/backward between form fields
- If a view has no tabs, `Tab` must do nothing (or be ignored)

**`↑ / ↓` — navigation between fields**
- The only keys to move focus from one field to another in a form
- In a list/table outside a form: row-by-row movement (Rule 111)

**`Space` — toggle checkbox**
- The only valid key to check/uncheck a checkbox
- Match it as `keymap.Space`, never as a `" "` literal (Bubble Tea v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`; `keymap.Space` is `"space"`); `TestNoKeyIsComparedToALiteralSpace` fails on a literal
- Reference implementation: `LaunchForm` (`internal/ui/oci_resources`), pinned by `launch_form_keys_test.go` — `TestLaunchFormSpaceTogglesEachCheckbox`, `TestLaunchFormDetachAndInteractiveExcludeEachOther`, `TestLaunchFormEnterNeverTogglesACheckbox`
- `Enter` on a checkbox must be ignored or advance to the next field, never toggle it
- **Confirmation buttons are the mirror case**: `Space` never answers Yes or No. `components.ConfirmModal`, `ChoiceModal`, `OptionConfirmModal` and the setup wizard's confirmation answer on `enter` only (plus `y`/`n` on the yes/no ones). In `OptionConfirmModal`, `space` toggles the option checkbox when it has focus (inert when locked) and `enter` on that checkbox is ignored

**`Enter` — validation / action**
- Validates the currently focused button
- Triggers a contextual action (e.g. launch a scan, open a detail view)
- Must **not** toggle a checkbox

**`← / →` — table navigation and value cycling**
- In a table: `←` moves up a level (drill up), `→` moves down a level (drill down)
- On a closed-list field (cycle field): `←` previous value, `→` next value (Rule 132)
- Must **not** move focus between form fields

#### Common violations to avoid

```go
// ❌ WRONG — Tab to navigate between fields
case "tab":
    m.focusedField = (m.focusedField + 1) % fieldCount

// ❌ WRONG — Enter to toggle a checkbox
case "enter":
    if m.focusedField == fieldMyCheckbox {
        m.myCheckbox = !m.myCheckbox
    }

// ✅ CORRECT — Space to toggle
case keymap.Space:
    if m.focusedField == fieldMyCheckbox {
        m.myCheckbox = !m.myCheckbox
    }

// ✅ CORRECT — ↑/↓ to navigate between fields
case "up":
    m.focusedField = max(m.focusedField-1, 0)
case "down":
    m.focusedField = min(m.focusedField+1, fieldCount-1)
```

### Rule 140 : An invalid field is underlined, and the footer says why (DEVDESK-292)

**A field that fails validation gets a wavy red underline, and the same error is in the footer. The underline is never the only carrier.**

- **One entry point.** The underline comes from `theme.StyleInvalidField(base)` (curly underline, `UnderlineCurly`, colour `theme.ColorInvalidField`). Never call `Underline*` anywhere else: `TestGuardInvalidFieldUnderlineHasOneEntryPoint` fails the suite. For a `textinput` use `theme.SetTextInputInvalid(&ti, invalid)`; for a `WrappedInput`, `SetInvalid(bool)`.
- **Colour.** `theme.ColorInvalidField` is a closed alias of `ColorFooterError` (no theme key, Rule 119). Its contrast against `ColorBackground` is at least 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11), tested on every shipped theme.
- **The message is in the footer, level Error (Rule 128)**, taken from `components.Validation.Status()`. It is derived on every render, so it does not vanish after 3 s like a timed `footer.Error()`. The parent view returns it from its status function while the form is open.
- **Nothing is invalid before the first refused submit.** After it, every change revalidates the whole form (`Validation.Revalidate`) and the footer follows.
- **A required field left empty:** its placeholder is underlined. A focused empty `WrappedInput` shows a cursor, not its placeholder: nothing to underline, the footer carries the message.
- **Spaces are not underlined** (`UnderlineSpaces(false)`), otherwise the `textinput` padding would be underlined across the whole width. A value made only of spaces is therefore not underlined: the footer is the only carrier.
- **Restyle on a change of state only.** `SetTextInputInvalid` resets the cursor blink (`IsBlinked` goes back to false), so calling it on every message freezes the cursor. Go through `components.InvalidMarks.Sync(key, &ti, invalid)`, from `Update()` only (Rule 110), never from `View()` or a `Cmd`.
- **Prefix unchanged.** The focus prefix `●` stays as in Rule 120. The underline adds no cell: the rendered width does not change.
- **Fallback.** A terminal without styled underlines gets a plain underline (SGR 4), still readable. Cost: about 60 bytes per underlined character. Risk: SGR 58 and `4:3` on old terminals, to check by hand.

```go
// ✅ CORRECT — state change only, in Update()
f.validation.Revalidate(f.errors())
f.marks.Sync(keyName, &f.nameInput, f.validation.Invalid(keyName))

// ❌ WRONG — a local underline, and a restyle on every message
f.nameInput.SetStyles(lipgloss.NewStyle().Underline(true)...)
theme.SetTextInputInvalid(&f.nameInput, true) // in every Update
```

Forms covered, and where the rules live: `docs/architecture/ui-components.md` ("Invalid form fields"). Out of scope: `templates/form.go`, netdiag, the `ctrl+p` palette, `FilterBar`.

Guards: `internal/ui/theme/source_guard_test.go` (`TestGuardNoHexColorOutsideColorsGo`, `TestGuardInvalidFieldUnderlineHasOneEntryPoint`, `TestGuardDetectors`).
